div.head: EGu 10
div.ab: Gif limlæweo lama, þe forworht wære, weorþe forlæten, ⁊ he æfter þam ðreo niht alibbe, siððan man mot hylpan be bisceopes leafe, se ðe wylle beorgan sare ⁊ saule.
Gyf limlǽpeo lama, ðe forworht wære, weorðe forlæten, ⁊ he æfter ðam ðreo niht alibbe, siððan mon mot hylpan be bisceopes leafe, se ðe wylle beorgan sare ⁊ saule.
Si límeþeo lama, qui forisfactus esset, dimittatur et ipse uiuat tres noctes, potest ei deinceps subueniri per episcopi licentiam, si quis uelit.

Si quis forisfactus et de membris disfactus dimittatur et idem post afflictionem suam tres noctes uiuat, potest ei deinceps per episcopi licentiam subueniri, si quis eius doloribus condescendat et anime.
Gif limlæweo lama, þe forworht wære, weorþe forlæten, ⁊ he æfter þam ðreo niht alibbe, siððan man mot hylpan be bisceopes leafe, se ðe wylle beorgan sare ⁊ saule.
Gif limlæwed lama þe forworht wære weorþe forlæten and he æfter þam ðreo niht alibbe, siððan man mot hylpan be bisceopes leafe, se ðe wylle beorgan sare and saule.

Wenn ein an Gliedern verstümmelter Krüppel, der [zur Hinrichtung] verurtheilt war, verlassen wird und nach dem drei Tage überlebt, dann darf mit des Bischofs Erlaubniss jemand [ihm] helfen, wer der Wunde und der Seele Rettung bringen will.

If a cripple mutilated in his limbs, who had been condemned [to execution], is abandoned and survives three days after that, then anyone who wishes to bring help to the wound and the soul may help [him] with the bishop’s permission.

If a criminal who has been mutilated and maimed is abandoned, and three days later he is still alive, after this time [has elapsed] he who wishes to have regard to his wounds and his soul may help him with the permission of the bishop.

If a mutilated man who might have been executed comes to be abandoned and he survives for three nights, afterward, with the bishop’s permission, anyone who wishes to heal his injuries and his soul might help him.

Neben Fem. limlæw ‘Verstümmelung’ setzen Toller und Sweet (dieser als aus *-læwa), danach mein Wb., ein Adj. læweo an. Die Endung, jedenfalls unnormal, drückt vielleicht nur den Instrum. jenes Fem. aus, so dass man das Adj. streichen und ‘durch Gliederverstümmelung lahm’ erklären dürfte. — Toller verbindet das Wort mit *gelewed; dieses erschliesst er aus Ælfrics Übertragung von (iumentum) debilitatum zu geleued, das Grein vielmehr als gelefed druckt. Toller Suppl. setzt mit alefian ‘schwächen, schädigen, verstümmeln, verkrüppeln’ alewian identisch; er zitiert Agsä. Bened. regel ed. Schröer 51 alewed für debile, wofür eine späte Hs. alyfed [vielleicht moderneres Synonym!] einführt. Sweet trennt den Stamm lef (‘krank, schwach; Schaden’) von læw. — Agsä. þ ward oft als p verlesen (s. Wb 170 Z. 1); also keine Beziehung zu læppa ‘Teil’!

Alongside the fem. limlæw ‘mutilation’, Toller and Sweet (the latter as from *-læwa), and following them my Wb., posit an adj. læweo. The ending, abnormal in any case, perhaps expresses merely the instrumental of that fem., so that the adj. could be deleted and the meaning explained as ‘lamed by mutilation of the limbs’. — Toller connects the word with *gelewed; he infers this from Ælfric’s rendering of (iumentum) debilitatum by geleued, which Grein, however, prints as gelefed. Toller Suppl. treats alewian as identical with alefian ‘weaken, harm, mutilate, cripple’; he cites Agsä. Bened. regel ed. Schröer 51 alewed for debile, for which a late MS introduces alyfed [perhaps a more modern synonym!]. Sweet separates the stem lef (‘sick, weak; harm’) from læw. — A.-S. þ was often misread as p (see Wb 170 l. 1); so there is no connection with læppa ‘part’!

Zwei Tage lang war also verboten, ärztlich dem nach der Verstümmelung drohenden Tode vorzubeugen; d. h. wie durch ‘ein Orakel’ ward Gott befragt, ob Verbrecher leben solle; Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 130; vgl. Gl Todesstrafe 1. 6. 7

For two days, therefore, it was forbidden to forestall by medical means the death threatening after the mutilation; i.e., God was consulted, as by ‘an oracle’, as to whether the criminal should live; Schreuer Verbrechenskonk. 130; cf. Gl Todesstrafe 1. 6. 7
